answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a river that only lets boats pass after paying a toll at the gate. A single identity that misbehaves loses its stake and its earned reputation, so an attacker who mirrors one honest agent into a thousand copies must fund a thousand stakes — the cost grows linearly while the gain stays flat. Over the horizon, honest agents accumulate history that cheap clones cannot fake, making forgery expensive and honesty the profitable strategy.
